 Judgment

Initially, the present petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs. 1,00,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the minor petitioner in a road traffic accident, represented by her natural guardian and mother.
Subsequently, on the petitioner attaining the age of majority, the guardianship of her mother stood discharged, and the petitioner has since been prosecuting the case in her own capacity.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 25-01-2021 at about 9.15 a.m., she was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-41-EQ-1348 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") on Kengeri-Mysore Road, from Bidadi towards Nayandanahalli, Kengeri,
Bengaluru.
At that time, the said motorcycle came into collision with a KSRTC bus bearing registration No. KA-10-F- 0326, resulting in the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College and Hospital where she was given first aid.
Thereafter, she was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, where she underwent treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.
The petitioner has further contended that her parents incurred an expenditure of about Rs. 6,00,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment, and other incidental expenses.
4. It is her case that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.

She has also stated that at the time of the accident, she was a 10th standard student, and due to the injuries sustained, she is unable to sit or stand for more than 30 minutes, and is unable to concentrate on her studies.
She claims that this has resulted in permanent disability affecting her day-to- day life.
On these grounds, the petitioner has prayed that just and reasonable compensation be awarded against the respondents.
5. In response to the petition, notice was duly served and Respondent No.1 appeared through counsel and filed its written statement.
The name of Respondent No. 2 has been struck off as it is not a necessary party.
Respondent No. 3, who is the registered owner-cum-rider of the offending vehicle, has appeared before this Court through counsel, but has not filed any written statement.

6. Respondent No. 1 - Insurance Company, in its written statement, has specifically contended that the mandatory provisions under Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act have not been complied with either by the owner of the offending vehicle or by the concerned police authorities.

While admitting that a policy of insurance had been issued in respect of the offending vehicle, it has been pleaded that the liability under the said policy is always subject to the terms and Yashawini.

It is further contended that the liability of the insurance company, if any, is subject to the condition that the driver of the offending vehicle held a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
7. It is also the specific defence of the insurer that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC bus, and not due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
Further, the insurer has contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of accident.

The insurance company has also disputed the nature and extent of injuries, the alleged disability, as well as the medical expenditure claimed by the petitioner, and has further contended that the compensation sought is highly excessive and exaggerated.
On these grounds, Respondent No. 1 has sought for dismissal of the petition.

8. Additionally, Respondent No. 1 has filed an additional written statement, wherein it is contended that it had issued a policy in favour of the third respondent in respect of the offending vehicle for the period from 13-08-2019 to 12-08-2024, the first year being from 13-08-2019 to 12-08-2020.

Respondent No.1 has clarified that the said policy covered only the risk of third parties, and a stand-alone two-wheeler own-damage policy had separately been issued by Royal Sundaram General Insurance for the period from 02-10-2020 to 01-10-2021.
It is specifically pleaded that no additional premium was paid to cover the risk of a pillion rider.
Therefore, Respondent No. 1 has contended that it is not liable to indemnify the claim in respect of the petitioner, who was admittedly a pillion rider at the time of accident.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained injuries when she was a pillion rider in motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EQ- 1348 on 25-01-2021 about 9.15 a.m. Kengeri-Mysuru road, towards Bidadi to Nayandalli, Masidi Kengeri, Bengaluru District, only due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the said motorcycle?
2. What compensation petitioner is entitled ?
3. What order ?

10. In order to prove the claim, the mother of Petitioner examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.9.
11.

Respondent- insurance company has examined its official as RW-1 and copy of policy is marked at Ex.R.1.
12.

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:

sentences.text: Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 13. ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 25-01-2021 at about 9.15 a.m., she was proceeding as a pillion rider on the offending vehicle on Kengeri-Mysore Road, from Bidadi towards Nayandanahalli, Kengeri, Bengaluru.
At that time, the said motorcycle came into collision with a KSRTC Bus bearing registration No. KA-10-F-0326, resulting in the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

14. In order to substantiate her case, mother of petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 6 i.e., FIR, complaint, wound certificate, spot sketch, rough sketch and charge sheet.
As per wound certificate petitioner has sustained the following injuries in the accident.

i) A 2 cm laceration infra orbital region on the right side,
ii)cut injury measuring 2" over the right parietal region.
Doctor has opined that injuries are simple in nature.
15. Initially, Respondent No. 1 had taken a contention that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC driver and not on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

However, subsequently, in its additional written statement, Respondent No. 1 taken its stand and raised the defence that although the motorcycle was insured, the insurance policy did not cover the risk of a pillion rider as on the date of the accident.
It was further contended that no additional premium had been paid to cover such risk, and therefore, the insurer was not liable to indemnify the claim of the petitioner.

16. During the course of cross-examination, learned counsel for Respondent No. 1 specifically suggested to PW1 that the accident had occurred solely due to negligence of the driver of the KSRTC bus and not on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
However, when a specific question was put forth by the Court, PW1 stated that the accident occurred due to negligence of her husband.
Except for above stray admission, Respondent No. 1 has not placed any cogent material on record to prove its plea that the accident was caused due to negligence of the KSRTC driver.

17. On the contrary, the police documents produced by the petitioner at Exhibits P1 to P7, namely FIR, complaint,wound certificate, spot mahazar, spot sketch, and charge sheet, consistently attribute negligence to the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The charge sheet filed after due investigation by the police against the rider of the motorcycle is a strong piece of contemporaneous evidence supporting the case of the petitioner.
18. It is a well-settled principle that in proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act, the Tribunal is not required to insist on the strict standard of proof applicable in criminal trials.
Instead, the test of preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Mere suggestions in cross-examination, without Yashawini.

sentences.text: 19. In the present case, the version of PW1 stands corroborated by the contemporaneous police records.
No independent witness or documentary evidence has been adduced by Respondent No. 1 to substantiate its allegation that the accident occurred due to negligence of the KSRTC driver.
Similarly, Respondent No. 3, though a father of the petitioner and party to the proceedings, has not produced any evidence to disprove the case.
20. Accordingly, this Tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
As a result of this accident, the petitioner, who was a pillion rider, sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.2 :- As discussed in issue No.1 that it was the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
So far as quantum of compensation is concerned the PW-1 has stated that she has spent more than 6,00,000/- towards treatment, medical, food and conveyance and other incidental expenses.
It is found that the Petitioner has sustained a 2 cm laceration infra orbital region on the right side, cut injury measuring 2" over the right parietal region.
Doctor has opined that injuries are simple in nature.
PW-1 has stated that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Nimhans hospital, Bengaluru from 26-01- 2021 to 18-02-2021 for 24 days and she has produced discharge summary at Ex.P7.
On perusal of charge sheet and wound certificate, it is seen that the petitioner sustained only simple injuries.
However discharge shows that the date of admission on 26/1/2021 and date of discharge on 18/2/2021.
the date of discharge shows handwritten insertion while rest of the contents are computerized.
No case sheet, inpatient records or treatment file has been produced to substantiate the entries found in the discharge summary.
In the absence of such corroborative material, the discharge summary does not inspire confidence of the tribunal.
It creates reasonable doubt regarding the genuineness of the said document.
At the time of the accident, she was a 10th standard student, and due to the injuries sustained, she is unable to sit or stand for more than 30 minutes, and is unable to concentrate on her studies.
She claims that this has resulted in permanent disability affecting her day-to-day life.
In support her education PW-1 has not produced the documents.
She has not examined the doctor to prove the permanent disability suffered by her.
Absolutely there is no disability stated and there is no evidence that the injuries has affected her day to day activities.
PW-1 has produced medical bills at Ex.P.8 amounting to Rs.1,65,664/-.

Considering the nature of injury, treatment taken by Petitioner, her age and the date of accident, I deem it proper to award 2,00,000/- of global compensation under all the conventional heads, as the Petitioner has suffered some sort of pain and had to take treatment for her injuries.
22. Liability:
Respondent No. 1 in its additional written statement has raised a comprehensive defence relating to the nature and scope of the insurance coverage.

The core of the contention is that while the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EQ-1348 was insured, the nature of policies issued does not extend to cover the petitioner who was a pillion rider at the time of accident.

It is specifically contended that Respondent No. 1 issued a third-party liability policy in respect of the Yashawini.S vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45354991/

sentences.text: Respondent No. 2 issued a separate stand-alone own damage policy through Royal Sundaram General Insurance under Policy No. VMSS0003552000100 valid from 02.10.2020 to 01.10.2021.
Both policies cover only the statutory risks as per law.
The third-party liability policy covers third parties on the road, but no additional premium was paid to cover the risk of a pillion rider.
The stand- alone own damage policy protects only the insured motorcycle against damage, but does not extend to pillion riders or third parties.

23. Thus, the entire defence of Respondent No. 1 rests on the plea that although the motorcycle was duly insured, the petitioner, being a pillion rider, does not fall within the category of "third party"
for whom coverage was available under the policy produced.

In absence of an additional premium,
the contractual and statutory liability of the insurer cannot be extended to the pillion rider.
24. The tribunal has carefully considered this defence.
From the documents produced, it is evident that the insurance coverage consisted of a long-term third-party policy and a stand-alone own damage policy.
The former was statutory in nature, but the scope of third-party liability in relation to pillion riders.
Unless specifically extended by payment of an additional premium, the insurer is not liable to indemnify claims in respect of pillion riders.
The latter, being a stand-alone own damage policy, does not cover any third-party risks, much less pillion riders.
25. The petitioner has not produced any evidence to demonstrate that an additional premium was paid for coverage of a pillion rider.
Nor has any endorsement or rider on the insurance policy been produced to rebut the contention of the insurer.
In such a situation, the tribunal has no reason to disbelieve the specific defence raised by Respondent No. 1.

Accordingly, this tribunal finds that Respondent No. 1 has succeeded in substantiating its plea that the insurance policies in force at the time of accident did not extend coverage to the petitioner, who was a pillion rider.

Therefore,
Respondent No. 1 cannot be fastened with liability to indemnify the petitioner under the policies issued.
The liability, if any, would rest with the owner and rider of the offending motorcycle, subject to further determination of negligence.

Respondent No.3 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petition against the respondent No.1 is dismissed.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.3 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount with interest shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
